## Why This Is Asked

This tests CGO memory ownership, safe streaming boundaries, and concurrent processing of stateful C resources from Go.

## Key Concepts

- Go-C memory ownership and free_token contract
- Opaque C handles lifecycles
- Streaming parsers: chunked input, token boundaries
- Concurrency: multi-stream worker pool, channel piping
- Error propagation across boundaries and resource cleanup
- Testing: race, partial token, cancellation

## Code Example

```c
int push_chunk(ParserHandle*, const char* chunk, size_t len);
char* next_token(ParserHandle*, size_t* token_len, int* is_complete);
void free_token(char* token);
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of CGO memory ownership, two-pass C APIs, and proper error mapping.

## Key Concepts
- CGO memory ownership across Go/C
- Two-pass buffer sizing and safe allocation
- Errno to Go error translation
- Concurrency safety with separate buffers
- Data marshaling between C and Go

## Code Example
Header declaration: int format_report(const char* name, const int* data, size_t n, char* out, size_t out_len);

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this to stream large data without two allocations?
